clue.text: Colonel retreats, accepting soldier's reasoning

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation takes in, or accepts, the soldier's letters within it
something that retreats goes backwards, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: Col is the standard abbreviation for the rank of colonel
GI is the familiar name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An officer backs down after hearing out a private's line of argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' reverses the colonel's abbreviation to give LOC, and 'accepting' wraps that around the American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the science of sound thinking, so it is a fair synonym for a chain of argument.

clue.text: His unpunctuality damages morale, etc

indicators.note: damages means the letters of morale and etc are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A colleague's habit of turning up late wears down the team's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damages' rearranges MORALE and ETC. The whole clue describes the person, whose lateness lowers everyone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arrives after the appointed time is the one whose lack of punctuality causes the trouble.

clue.text: Pained reaction when an elderly relative takes nothing in

indicators.note: in, after takes, means the zero goes inside the relative's word

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother
the letter O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An old family member gets nothing and lets out a sigh of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... in' puts O inside GRAN; 'takes' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a deep sound made in pain or displeasure.

clue.text: Principal sort of heating

definitions.meaning: main or chief, as in the ... argument
a household system that heats a whole building from one boiler

explanation.definitionFit: Central means chief or most important, and central heating warms a home from one source.

clue.text: Claim pier has been vandalized -it's based on observation

indicators.note: something vandalized has been smashed about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that the seaside pier has been damaged by hooligans, and the claim rests on what was seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been vandalized' scrambles the letters of CLAIM and PIER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge comes from experiment and experience rather than theory.

clue.text: A little boy has it — or a journalist

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small child has something, or perhaps a reporter does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little boy' gives the shortened name ED; IT and OR are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor works in journalism, preparing and choosing material for a newspaper.

clue.text: College student got round it, speaking several languages

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of British college

indicators.note: the word got goes round the student's letter

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A university student managed to get by by speaking many tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a former type of British college, later made a university. 'round' wraps the verb around the learner's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot has mastery of many tongues.

clue.text: Go berserk and violently strike attendant

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a page is a boy servant or attendant

explanation.surface: Someone loses control and lashes out at a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go berserk' is a verb, and the answer works as a verb here too.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about wildly and destructively.

clue.text: Colouring for fowl and fish, say

parts.note: the Cochin is a breed of large domestic chicken

indicators.note: say signals the next word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: the eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: Dye for poultry and seafood, perhaps used in cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: COCHIN is a chicken breed; 'say' turns EEL into the spoken EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: A Fellow in the meadow covered with greenery

indicators.note: in places A and the fellow's letter inside the meadow word

parts.note: ley is an old word for a meadow, a variant of lea
F is the abbreviation for Fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A college member stands in a green field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and F inside LEY, an old word for a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in leaves is lush with foliage.

clue.text: A small bird initially threatened by a large one

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word threatened

parts.note: a large bird, picking up 'bird' from the definition: the hornbill is a big tropical bird with a huge beak

explanation.surface: A little bird is menaced by a bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: The small Australian thornbill is the large hornbill with the first letter of 'threatened' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The thornbill is a tiny Australasian songbird, a type of warbler.

clue.text: Alternative drink served after instant coffee

indicators.note: the drink's letters come after, or follow, those for an instant

parts.note: a mo, short for moment, is an instant
cha is the alternative spelling of char, slang for tea

explanation.surface: Instead of something else, a beverage is offered once the instant coffee is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant coffee' reads as one phrase, but 'instant' gives MO and 'coffee' alone is the definition. CHA is a variant of CHAR, British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a strong coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: We can bank on our balance being secure when this is low

definitions.text: We can bank on our balance being secure when this is low

parts.words: We can bank on our balance being secure when this is low
parts.note: reads like a remark about money in the bank, but 'bank' means to tilt and 'balance' means physical stability: an object is steadiest when the point its weight acts through sits low

explanation.surface: A customer is assured their bank account is safe as long as something stays low.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial words 'bank' and 'balance' mislead: a vehicle banking on a turn stays upright when its weight is concentrated low down.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics term for the point through which an object's weight acts; the lower it sits, the more stable the object.

clue.text: Letter from abroad lies in mess on the breakfast table

definitions.note: a phrase, not a noun: it describes the answer by where it is found

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled, so the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign letter is lying among the clutter at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' could be any foreign letter; the Greek one fits. 'in mess' scrambles the lying word into ESLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Record one specific article about the old philosopher

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase meaning relating to the old philosopher

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
the Roman numeral I is one
a specific is a medicine for a particular illness, a cure
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone writes down one exact piece about an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specific' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, a remedy. 'about' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicurean means relating to Epicurus, the Greek thinker who held pleasure the highest good.

clue.text: One fated, possibly, to be unreliable on the pitch?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A footballer seems doomed to be unreliable on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONE and FATED. 'Pitch' suggests a sports field; here it means musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tone-deaf cannot tell musical notes apart, so cannot be trusted to sing in tune.

clue.text: This food might satisfy, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the phrase is heard, not seen

parts.note: might is force, power, and to satisfy a need is to meet it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a dish ought to be filling, judging by its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun FORCE, and 'satisfy' is MEET, as in meeting a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcemeat is a stuffing of chopped meat and seasoning.

clue.text: Strong player takes a wedge, perhaps

parts.note: a cast is the group of players in a show
a wedge is one example of a golf iron, a club with a metal head

explanation.surface: A powerful golfer selects a wedge for the shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says a wedge is one example of an IRON. 'Strong' looks like it describes the player but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is very hard, so it describes something firm and unbreakable, as in a cast-iron alibi.

clue.text: Protective clothing, made by a trendy firm, seen in desert

indicators.note: the first letters are seen inside the word for desert

parts.note: to desert is to rat, as one rats on a cause
in means fashionable, as in the in thing
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A fashionable company makes protective clothing that turns up in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun for sand and dunes, but it is the verb meaning to abandon a cause. 'seen in' places the three short pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat keeps the wearer dry in wet weather.

clue.text: Firm container holding fine sea-food

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the container holds the letter for fine inside it

parts.note: a dish holds food
F stands for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A company sells a dish of good-quality fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts F inside DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is an edible fish caught in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: He strolls about heading the rose-tree

indicators.note: heading means beheading here: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a rambler is a climbing rose

explanation.surface: A man walks round, leading the way to the rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay. 'heading' means beheading: RAMBLER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambler walks at a slow, relaxed pace, wandering here and there.

clue.text: Lawgiver almost gulping a measure of wine

indicators.note: gulping means the shortened name swallows the measure
almost means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Mount Sinai
the ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Moses nearly downs a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the lawgiver's name, giving MOSE; 'gulping' swallows the old length measure into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a German white wine from the Moselle valley.

clue.text: The least successful position for a weaver

definitions.meaning: the lowest place in a league or class
Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.definitionFit: The lowest place in a ranking, and the name of Shakespeare's weaver who is given an ass's head.

clue.text: Cast violently into a street, one may be laid flat and low

definitions.text: may be laid flat and low

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould

indicators.note: violently means the letters of 'into a' are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something hurled into the road may end up lying flat on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like part of 'cast violently', but it gives FOUND alone; 'violently' rearranges INTO A to ATION. The 'one' that is laid is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation stone is a block set at ground level, often with ceremony, at the base of a new building.

clue.text: Gathering excitement for an imperfect speaker.

indicators.note: someone with a speech impediment may say F where TH belongs

parts.note: a thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement

explanation.surface: A speaker who struggles with words still builds up excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Many speakers say F for TH ('fing' for 'thing'), turning THRILL into FRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a strip of fabric gathered along one edge for decoration.

clue.text: American Indian people without a wise man?

parts.note: without suggests none at all, the letter O as a zero
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A tribe finds itself lacking a wise elder.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: O SAGE, read as 'zero sage', is a group with no wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American nation, originally from the Missouri valley.

clue.text: Old people appearing in a show twice nightly

indicators.note: the answer shows up, or appears, inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Elderly performers take part in a show staged two times each evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twICE NIghtly' holds the answer. The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient tribe of eastern Britain, so a people of long ago.

clue.text: Even the score after returning, before one has a tea-break

indicators.note: before puts the reversed piece ahead of what follows
returning means the word for after is read backwards

parts.note: later means after
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: a break here means the letters of tea are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A team pulls level later in the match, just before everyone stops for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea-break' reads as one word, but the hyphen splits fodder from indicator: 'break' scrambles the drink, while 'returning' turns the word for after back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to pay back an injury, settling the account with an opponent.

clue.text: A rare element discovered initially in Los Angeles

definitions.text: A rare element discovered initially in Los Angeles

parts.words: A rare element discovered initially in Los Angeles
parts.note: reads as a claim about where an element was found, but it says the element's name begins with the abbreviation of Los Angeles, and its Greek root means lying hidden, so 'discovered' is a joke

explanation.surface: Scientists first found an uncommon element in a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: It was really found in Sweden. The name opens with LA, and comes from Greek for 'lie hidden'. It is one of the rare earth metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft silvery metal, the first of the lanthanides, the rare earth elements.

clue.text: Exercise right to follow river

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right comes after the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone claims a right to walk along the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to use or apply.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert power or influence is to put it to use.
